set.body:
effectagram exports 78 symbols (NAMESPACE, 78 export() lines) with no signal anywhere about which are the entry path and which are expert or internal-facing surface. A newcomer reading the reference index meets compile_metric_schedule, materialize_metric, metric_training_policy, residual_pair_statistics, reconstruct_evidence, variation_query, pairing_marginals, numerical_contract, and coherent_functional on equal footing with relation, geometry, contrast, and rdm.

Comparative evidence, from the owner's own package. rMVPA solves this explicitly with a declared lifecycle surface at R/api_lifecycle.R:11-31, naming 13 stable functions:

  mvpa_config, build_analysis, run_analysis, save_results, install_cli,
  validate_analysis, mvpa_dataset, mvpa_design, load_model, mvpa_model,
  run_searchlight, run_regional, run_global

Everything else in rMVPA is exported but unregistered, so a reader knows where the supported path is. Its pkgdown reference is also grouped by task (_pkgdown.yml:8-62: Get Started, Core Concepts, Standard MVPA, RSA, REMAP, Extensibility) rather than alphabetically.

effectagram has neither device. There is no _pkgdown.yml at all, so the reference renders alphabetically, which puts abstract_domain and additive_frame first and buries geometry, contrast, rdm, and rsa in the middle of a flat list of 78.

The cost is specifically a cost of ABUNDANCE, and it is worth being precise that this is not a criticism of the exports themselves. The surface is large because the framework genuinely decomposes the problem finely, and most of these functions exist because a real distinction needed a name. The failure is that the package offers a newcomer no way to defer the distinctions they do not yet need. Precision that is optional-until-needed reads as precision that is mandatory-up-front when everything is presented at once.

Cheapest fixes, roughly in order of leverage per unit of risk:

  1. a _pkgdown.yml reference grouped by task. Pure presentation, changes no code,
     no semantics, no check surface. Should be near-free and is the obvious first move.
  2. a named entry set in the README - 'these six functions are the supported path,
     the rest are for when you need them'
  3. optionally an api_lifecycle-style declaration mirroring rMVPA's convention

Explicitly NOT proposing deprecating or unexporting anything. The 0.1 chain justified this surface and none of the accessibility evidence so far argues any of it should go away. This is a navigation problem, not a scope problem.
set.title: No tiering of the 78 exports: a newcomer cannot tell the 6 functions they need from the 72 they do not
